work.title: Sentiment Analysis of Call Center Conversations
work.tagline: Converting the storm of customer voices into actionable intelligence.
work.intro: In the heart of the claims department, every call is a life interrupted. This project built an end-to-end NLP pipeline to perceive the emotions behind words — transforming thousands of daily customer service conversations into structured, supervisable sentiment signals.
responsibilities: Used data analysis and stakeholder interviews to uncover pain points and identify problems within the existing business workflow
Designed and implemented a full sentiment analysis pipeline from raw call transcripts
Leveraged different pretrained AI API, reviewing and refining the generated outputs to organize and consolidate meaningful insights

selectedWork.title: The Challenge: Drowning in the Queue
selectedWork.overview: High call volumes, repeated transfers, and emotionally charged customers created an unmanageable noise problem. Supervisors had no systematic view of sentiment trends across their teams.
selectedWork.role: Defined the problem scope, audited existing workflows, and identified key sentiment signals worth extracting.

images.caption: The Challenge: call queue overload and emotional noise
The sea of voices — fragmented caller perspectives

selectedWork.overview: Built a multi-class sentiment classifier to detect emotional states — churn risk, renewal anxiety, frustration, neutral satisfaction — from transcript text, with confidence scoring per utterance.
selectedWork.role: Led model selection, fine-tuning, and evaluation. Designed the output schema for downstream dashboard consumption.

selectedWork.title: Sentiment Hub: Wisdom from Noise
selectedWork.overview: Designed a supervisor-facing dashboard that displays real-time sentiment monitoring by territory, flags at-risk accounts, and surfaces AI-generated recommendations for agent intervention.
selectedWork.role: End-to-end design and implementation of the data pipeline feeding the dashboard, including territory-level aggregation and alert logic.

images.caption: Supervisor Sentiment Hub — macro view of voice data

work.reflection: This project shifted the team's mental model from reacting to phone queues to anticipating sentiment. The biggest challenge was bridging the gap between model accuracy and operational trust — supervisors needed interpretable outputs, not just scores.

work.title: Behavior Flow Visualization
work.tagline: Tracing the invisible paths users leave behind.
work.intro: User journeys through digital environments are rarely linear. This project built an interactive visualization system to map, cluster, and interpret how users navigate complex platforms — turning raw behavioral sequences into legible flow diagrams for product and UX teams.
responsibilities: Processed raw event-log data into structured behavioral sequences
Designed and implemented interactive flow visualization using D3.js
Identified dominant navigation patterns and friction points through clustering
Delivered findings as an interactive dashboard for non-technical stakeholders

selectedWork.title: Data Processing & Sequence Extraction
selectedWork.overview: Cleaned and structured millions of event-log entries into user session sequences, applying deduplication, session boundary detection, and event taxonomy normalization.
selectedWork.role: Sole data engineer and analyst for the preprocessing pipeline.

selectedWork.title: Flow Visualization Design
selectedWork.overview: Designed a Sankey/alluvial-style interactive flow diagram to display user path frequencies, drop-off points, and branching decision clusters across the platform.
selectedWork.role: Designed and coded the visualization from scratch, iterating on layout clarity through stakeholder feedback rounds.

selectedWork.title: Insight Delivery
selectedWork.overview: Translated business workflow logic into code to track user transitions across stages, aligning node counts with SQL data warehouse records and visualizing the process through a real-time Sankey diagram connected to the database.
selectedWork.role: Authored the insight narrative and presented findings to product stakeholders.

work.reflection:
I believe the most important aspect of this work is that both the visualization and the analysis are closely aligned with the business context. Effective visualization requires selecting the most appropriate format to communicate specific information. I experimented with several alternative visualizations, but none of them conveyed the user’s browsing behavior and decision-making process as intuitively as the final Sankey diagram.

One aspect I believe could be improved further is highlighting the nodes related to the purchasing decision while still maintaining the overall clarity and simplicity of the visualization.
